channel.title: The Coin Wire
channel.description: Crypto news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, DeFi, stablecoins, exchanges, regulation and protocol upgrades: what changed, and what comes next.

item.title: Anyswap routes depended on token and destination liquidity
item.description: Anyswap’s former router and bridge routes differed by token representation and destination liquidity; the service ceased operations, so route choice is no longer live.

item.title: Mantle Bridge or an Exchange? The Cost of an Occasional Transfer
item.description: For occasional transfers to Mantle, the canonical bridge preserves the asset and wallet control; an exchange may simplify cash-out but adds custody and conversion steps.

item.title: BlackRock’s IBIT drove $526.6 million Bitcoin ETF inflow
item.description: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $526.6 million on Oct. 19, but BlackRock’s IBIT alone added more than the group net as rival funds recorded withdrawals.

item.title: How QuickSwap Integrations Handle Swaps and Liquidity
item.description: QuickSwap integrations route trades and liquidity through version-specific contracts; the key choice is whether broad V2 pools or concentrated V3 positions suit the product.

item.title: A Cross-Chain Transfer Won’t Renew Storage on Its Own
item.description: Funding a storage renewal from another chain means delivering the required asset to the storage network, then submitting renewal there; the transfer alone changes nothing.

item.title: JPMorgan Extends JPM Coin to Ethereum Mainnet
item.description: JPMorgan has deployed its deposit token on Ethereum for institutional clients, widening its public-chain reach beyond Base while keeping access restricted.

item.title: JPMorgan brings JPM Coin to Ethereum mainnet
item.description: JPMorgan has made its dollar deposit token available to institutions on Ethereum, adding a public network beside Base for onchain payments and settlement.

item.title: Borderless’s 84% remittance saving meets a route-by-route test
item.description: Borderless puts a $200 stablecoin-funded remittance at $2, against $12.72 for traditional transfers, but the comparison spans different periods and costs vary by route.

item.title: Ledger reviews reseller controls after wallet implant attack
item.description: Ledger is reviewing reseller and anti-tamper controls after an implant was found in a CryptoBilis-sold wallet; trackers estimate losses above $93 million.

item.title: Ledger reviews reseller controls after wallet implant thefts
item.description: Ledger is reviewing reseller sales and anti-tamper controls after implanted devices tied to about $90 million in losses exposed a gap in its integrity checks.

item.title: Deutsche Bank plans Germany custody launch, Asia expansion in 2027
item.description: Deutsche Bank says its German crypto custody service is weeks from launch, with Asian expansion planned for 2027 as it builds beyond traditional banking rails.

item.title: Coinbase and Marqeta add stablecoin-backed cards for businesses
item.description: Coinbase will custody stablecoin balances and convert them to fiat for Marqeta-issued cards, adding an enterprise route to spend digital dollars across card networks.

item.title: A bridge change does not move a rollup treasury’s assets
item.description: A bridge update does not move treasury balances by itself. Map token contracts, compare withdrawal and liquidity routes, then migrate in verified stages.

item.title: Bitcoin and EVM swaps need different routes
item.description: Bitcoin transfers spend UTXOs and pay by transaction size; EVM swaps execute contracts and need gas, so the right route depends on where the asset must end up.

item.title: Four checks before swapping a rebasing token
item.description: Before signing a rebasing-token swap, check the asset, balance model, route support and execution limits; each can change what arrives and how much you keep.

item.title: A Practical Method for Settling Cross-Chain Crypto Invoices
item.description: Settle a cross-chain crypto invoice by fixing its value, naming the destination chain and agreeing who bears conversion, transfer and timing risk upfront.

item.title: Why bridged stablecoins can trade below their local peg
item.description: Bridged stablecoins can slip below a dollar when redemption routes, liquidity or trust differ from the issuer-backed token, even if both share a ticker.

item.title: A crypto swap resets the cost basis of both sides
item.description: A crypto swap can realize a gain or loss and start a new basis for the asset received, so each trade needs its own value, fee and lot records.

item.title: Judge keeps Gemini’s $5 million CFTC order in force
item.description: A New York judge left Gemini’s $5 million CFTC consent order intact, rejecting both sides’ effort to lift its injunction after the agency disavowed the case.

item.title: Why Wallets Switch Networks Before a Bridge Signature
item.description: A wallet switches to a bridge’s required chain to prepare the right signing context; the network prompt alone does not approve or move funds.
